question: What layer of Earth's mantle lies beneath the lithosphere that has enough pressure and heat to allow rocks to flow like a liquid with a viscous, caramel-like consistency?
solution:
The correct answer is** __Asthenosphere.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** asthenosphere is the mechanically weak and ductile region** of the upper mantle of Earth.
 
• **The asthenosphere **layer of Earth's mantle lies beneath the lithosphere that has enough pressure and heat to allow rocks to flow like a liquid with a viscous, caramel-like consistency.
 
• It lies below the lithosphere, between** approx. 80 and 200 km below the surface.**
 
• **The lower boundary of the asthenosphere is not well defined.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• The mesosphere is the **third layer of the atmosphere.**
 
• The troposphere is the** first and lowest layer of the atmosphere of the Earth.**
 
• The exosphere is the** outermost layer of the earth's atmosphere. **
